subject: english-language
title: Language & Power Foundations Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll meet the core concepts behind how language carries power.
meta_desc: GCSE English Language & Power walkthrough — Fairclough, instrumental vs influential power.
final_note: You learned Fairclough's two power types and the basics of asymmetrical interactions.

concepts.def: Ability to control or influence others through language
Power that persuades or shapes opinion (ads)
Unequal exchange where one party holds power
Linguist who theorised about language and power
The person with control in an interaction

walkthroughs.body_html: Norman Fairclough split power into instrumental (authority) and influential (persuasion).

A judge sentencing a defendant. A teacher giving detention. A police officer giving an order.

The power comes from ROLE — not from what's said.

An advert, a sermon, a politician's speech, an opinion piece.

No authority — just words shaping minds.

mcqs.q: A judge passing sentence holds what kind of power?
options: Influential
Instrumental
Covert
Indirect

mcqs.q: A car advert persuading you to buy uses what kind of power?
options: Instrumental
Influential
Asymmetrical only
No power

mcqs.q: Is language change a sign of decline?
options: No — modern linguistics treats change as natural and continuous, not as decay. Every language has always been changing and will continue to.
Language change only happens in informal speech, not in writing.
Skinner believed children couldn't learn language until age five.
Language change shows that standards are falling and English is being ruined.

mcqs.q: What is overextension in child language?
options: Skinner believed children couldn't learn language until age five.
When a child applies a word more broadly than adults do — e.g. calling all four-legged animals 'dog' before learning distinct categories.
Overextension is when children use very long words they don't understand.
Overextension is when children speak too loudly.

mcqs.q: What is Skinner's behaviourist view of language acquisition?
options: Children learn language through imitation and operant conditioning — they are reinforced for correct utterances and corrected for errors.
Skinner believed children couldn't learn language until age five.
Skinner believed in an innate grammar module.
Overextension is when children speak too loudly.
